title: "Data Validation"
description: "The process of checking that data satisfies expected rules and quality requirements."
term: "Data Validation"
letter: "D"
category: "Data Systems"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Data validation checks whether data is shaped and populated as expected
before it is used. It can catch missing fields, invalid values, and
unexpected changes early.

## Technical explanation

Validation rules may cover schemas, types, ranges, uniqueness, null
rates, relationships between fields, and distribution expectations.
Checks can run at ingestion, during transformations, before model
training, and at inference time. Rules should reflect the data contract
and the consequences of invalid values.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Invalid or shifted inputs can corrupt training datasets, break pipelines,
and cause unexpected model behaviour. Automated validation makes data
assumptions observable and can prevent bad inputs from silently
propagating.

## How it works

Define expected properties, evaluate data against them, and report or
handle violations according to a policy. Some failures block a pipeline;
others generate warnings or route records for review. Validation results
should be logged and monitored.

## Practical example

A tabular feature pipeline can require a non-null timestamp, constrain an
age field to a plausible range, and alert if an expected category suddenly
disappears.

## Common misconceptions

- Passing validation does not prove that data is representative or
  unbiased.
- Rules can become outdated as legitimate data changes.
- Silently dropping all invalid records can hide important quality
  problems.
